reader.requirement: At 1985 a reference modification of a numeric (usage DISPLAY, signed or scaled), numeric edited, alphabetic or alphanumeric edited data-name-1 operates on the item's character positions exactly as if it were an alphanumeric redefinition of the same size (sign characters, embedded or separate, editing characters and all), both as a sender and as a receiver.
reader.edition-search: grep of RefModBinder.cs and Model/Place.cs for Edition., DialectLevel, CobolVersion, Permissive, Construct: only Edition.Error/Warning diagnostics, no switch; grep of src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Editions for ref.?mod: only the 2023 REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH directive (zero length, not this rule) and the UNSTRING/report-control introductions, none on this path.

reader.notes: RefModView wraps a usage-DISPLAY numeric item in NumericImagePlace (its character image) and slices it with RefModPlace; edited and alphabetic items are already character strings. Every probed form printed the stored characters, including the trailing overpunch (implementor's sign representation) and SIGN SEPARATE characters. A non-DISPLAY numeric is refused by RefModExclusion (SR1), outside this rule.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IV.4.3.8.4 whole (SR1 usage DISPLAY, GR1 sign-separate ordinal, GR2). The attack was the storage substrate: if a numeric DISPLAY item's slice were rebuilt from its VALUE rather than read from its character positions, it would differ from an alphanumeric REDEFINES of the same item. Probes at --std 85, each slice compared against an explicit REDEFINES X(n) of the same storage: rmA invalid digits written through the REDEFINES ('12AB' in 9(4)) -> N4(3:2)=[AB]; SIGN LEADING embedded -123 -> SL(1:1)=[J] equal to the image; trailing positive overpunch S9(3) 123 -> [C] equal to the image; scaled SVPP99 -.0012 -> [1K] equal to the image; numeric edited $$,$$9.99- -> equal to the image; receivers MOVE '9' TO SL(1:1) -> image [923], MOVE 'X' TO N4(K:1) -> [X2AB], MOVE ALL '7' TO N4(2:) -> [X777], MOVE ZERO TO ST(1:2) -> [00C], INSPECT N4(1:) REPLACING -> [X555]. rmB file record area (sequential record '1A3B5}' read into S9(5)V9) -> RN1(2:3)=[A3B] RN1(6:1)=[}]; a LINKAGE S9(4) BY REFERENCE -> L(1:3)=[123] L(4:1)=[M], MOVE '5' TO L(1:1) -> caller sees -5234; MOVE TE(K)(K:1) TO K with K=2 -> [5] (subscript and modifier evaluated before the store). Every slice is the item's stored characters. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR2  the text is in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR1  the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.3 SR1  the text is in SR1'.
